small_guidance:
- The conv kernel's innermost `for ic in tl.static_range(0, IC)` with IC=3 forces scalar loads per channel; restructure to load all IC channels as a vector (`tl.arange(0, IC_PAD)` with IC_PAD=4) and do a `tl.dot` between a [BLOCK_OC, IC_PAD] weight tile and [IC_PAD, BLOCK_OW] input tile per (kd,kh,kw).
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_OW (64, 128) and try BLOCK_OC fixed at 16 (matches OC exactly) with num_warps=4/8 — current BLOCK_OC is rounded up to 16 already but configs don't sweep it; also try num_stages=3-4 to overlap the triple-nested kd/kh/kw loop loads.
- In group_norm_hardswish, fuse the weight/bias loads outside the second pass by precomputing per-channel scale = w*rstd and shift = b - mean*rstd*w in registers (only C_per_G values, e.g. 4) so the second loop is one FMA per element instead of two loads + multiply-add.
large_guidance:
- Switch the conv_transpose3d from the current "gather" formulation (per output point, loop over kernel & input) to the canonical scatter-add via implicit GEMM: treat it as a GEMM where input [N, IC, ID*IH*IW] is multiplied by weight reshaped [IC, OC*KD*KH*KW], producing a "col" tensor that is scatter-added into output with stride/pad index math. With IC=3, OC=16, this is a tiny-K GEMM and a single-pass scatter-add kernel can amortize input loads across all (kd,kh,kw) outputs.
- Alternatively, keep the gather form but make the program tile over (oc_block, od, oh, ow_block) with channels_last output layout so the OC=16 axis is contiguous and the store is a single 16-wide vector; this also lets the next kernel read groups (4 channels each) coalesced.
- Fuse the entire pipeline (conv_transpose + swish + group_norm + hardswish) by having the conv kernel write into shared/global buffers partitioned per (N, group), then a single persistent group-norm kernel that owns one (N,g) group does the two-pass reduction and hardswish — eliminates one full read/write of the OD*OH*OW*OC tensor (~4M elements/batch).
